clue.text: Church group's Oedipus complex

indicators.note: complex, in the sense of intricately tangled, tells us to rearrange the name before it

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst's joke that a Catholic organisation suffers from the famous Freudian syndrome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oedipus complex' reads as one Freudian phrase, but 'complex' is the anagram signal working on the seven letters of the name; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a Catholic institution founded in Spain in 1928, so it is a religious organisation within the Roman Church.

clue.text: Capital engineer turning up in middle of road

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other
middle of takes the central letters of road
turning up in a down entry means read from bottom to top

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine

explanation.surface: An engineer appears in the middle of the street in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turning up' means reading bottom to top; 'middle of road' keeps both central letters, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Retrospective, to some extent, for a mature artist of the floating world

indicators.note: Retrospective says the hidden letters are read backwards
to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gallery mounts a career retrospective for an elderly painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' looks like an exhibition but reverses the run ORAMATU hidden in 'for a mature'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitagawa Utamaro was a Japanese ukiyo-e printmaker; ukiyo-e means pictures of the floating world.

clue.text: Row with outsiders in race being held in low esteem

indicators.note: with here means having inside it, so the argument holds the next piece

parts.note: a row is a dispute or argument

indicators.note: outsiders in means the outer letters of the word race

explanation.surface: An argument with outsiders in a race lowers everyone's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: R and E, the outer letters of 'race', go inside DISPUTE; 'being held in' links, as in the phrase 'held in disrepute'.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepute is a state of having a bad reputation, so it means poor regard.

clue.text: Playwright dropping pence says truckers may use them

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for pence is let fall from the name

parts.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A dramatist, short of money, remarks on the habits of lorry drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Interstates are the US federal highways, used by long-distance truck drivers.

clue.text: Turner surpasses Brown

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or top it
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: An art critic ranks J. M. W. Turner above Ford Madox Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner and Brown look like two painters; Turner is the definition, a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship around which cable is wound, so it is something that rotates.

clue.text: Not real fish

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means mock or sham, as in a ... accent

explanation.definitionFit: Cod is British slang for fake as well as the name of a well-known food fish.

clue.text: King Edward, say, dismissing a primate

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato

explanation.surface: A monarch sends away a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks like a monarch, but it is a British potato variety; removing A from POTATO gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The potto is a slow-moving African primate related to lorises.

clue.text: Half of them being made redundant — anything considered

indicators.note: being made redundant means losing a job, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the second half of the word them
ought is a variant spelling of aught, meaning anything

explanation.surface: Half the workforce is laid off, and everything has been weighed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Making EM (half of 'them') redundant leaves TH; OUGHT is an old spelling of aught.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought as a past participle means pondered or reflected upon.

clue.text: Article supporting New English writer that caused sorrow to be forgotten

definitions.text: that caused sorrow to be forgotten

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means placed beneath the other pieces

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backs a fresh English author.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, nepenthe is a drug that banishes grief, a potion of forgetfulness.

clue.text: One's expelled from school, then given a placement and passed over

indicators.note: expelled from says the numeral one is thrown out of the word for school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
one is the Roman numeral I
something given a placement has been sited

explanation.surface: A pupil is expelled, then found a new school, and so moves across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled from' removes I (one) from TRAIN, leaving TRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To transit a place is to travel across or through it, so transited means crossed or passed over.

clue.text: Company having bad time in recession

indicators.note: something in recession is going backwards, so both pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: poor quality is bad quality

explanation.surface: A firm is struggling through hard times during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns POORT backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a body of soldiers, and a company is likewise a military unit or group of people.

clue.text: Swimmer in school with American astronomer

parts.note: George Ellery Hale was the American astronomer behind the Hale telescope

explanation.surface: A pupil swims at school alongside an American stargazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning: whales swim in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales travel in groups called schools, so a whale is a swimmer found in such a group.

clue.text: Gardener worried about old instrument

indicators.note: about says the reworked letters go around the next piece
worried, in the sense of fretted and pulled about, tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A gardener frets over something past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' shuffles GARDENER and 'about' wraps that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ, such as a harmonium, is a keyboard instrument sounded by vibrating reeds.

clue.text: Sergeant may revert to former state

indicators.note: revert suggests turning back into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier might return to how things were before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revert to' hints at going back in time, fitting a state that no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: East Germany, the German Democratic Republic, was a country that ceased to exist in 1990.

clue.text: Concur that post going astray is unsatisfactory

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a lost letter in the post is a poor show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astray' rearranges all fourteen letters of CONCUR THAT POST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not up to scratch fails to meet the expected standard, an idiom for inadequate.

clue.text: River trip must include old family member

indicators.note: must include says the word for trip holds the other pieces

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey
gran is a grandmother

explanation.surface: An outing must take along an elderly relative.
explanation.walkthrough: OGRAN goes inside RIDE after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is a major river forming part of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: One not coming out promises to pay for plant

parts.note: a scab is a strikebreaker who refuses to come out on strike
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker pledges to settle his debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' means joining a strike, as in British labour usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a flowering plant with pincushion-like heads, often blue or lilac.

clue.text: Unfinished business also includes disgusting musical work

indicators.note: unfinished says the word for business loses its final letter

parts.note: a concern is a business or firm

indicators.note: includes says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: too means also
gross means disgusting

explanation.surface: Incomplete business dealings also involve something revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the last letter of the word for business; 'includes' puts the disgusting word after the first two letters of the word for also.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto grosso is a Baroque orchestral form contrasting a small group of soloists with the full ensemble.

clue.text: For a Swedish soprano, nothing's like this nightingale's debut

parts.note: nil is nothing, with 's attached
so means in this way

indicators.note: debut means the first appearance, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A Swedish singer is compared to a songbird making its first appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a' links; 'debut' takes N from 'nightingale's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birgit Nilsson was a celebrated Swedish dramatic soprano known for Wagner roles.

clue.text: Work out what heir apparent should do

definitions.meaning: to work out is to turn out well or prosper
an heir apparent is expected to follow the current holder

explanation.definitionFit: Succeed means both to prosper and to follow someone into a title or office.

clue.text: Sheltered spot occupied by small tanker

indicators.note: occupied by says the next piece sits inside the first

parts.note: a bower is a shady leafy shelter

explanation.surface: A small lorry parks in a shady nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowser is a mobile tank for fuel or water, the name coming from a US maker of pumps.

clue.text: Wise man — one from northern Europe — developed a rash

parts.note: a Balt is a native of the Baltic states such as Latvia or Lithuania

indicators.note: developed suggests something changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian sage comes out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges A RASH into HASAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Balthasar is traditionally named as one of the three Magi who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: What about ram getting agitated?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what
tup is a dialect word for a ram

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is getting a sheep worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses EH; 'getting' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being het up means being anxious or excited, an informal phrase for flustered.

clue.text: Clergyman ultimately wanting page three, for example

indicators.note: ultimately wanting means lacking the final letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar eventually seeks a topless tabloid feature.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'page three' evokes the Sun's notorious pin-up page; here it is just any odd-numbered page.
explanation.definitionFit: A recto is a right-hand page of a book, which always carries an odd number such as three.

clue.text: Cricket side prepared for attack

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: A cricket team is ready to go on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or onslaught, as well as a beginning.

clue.text: Goofy one's left bone dry

indicators.note: left here means has gone out of, so the word one departs from bone

parts.note: the word one, with 's meaning has
a rainless spell is a dry one

explanation.surface: Disney's dog leaves a bone lying in the drought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's left bone' means 'one has left bone': remove ONE from BONE to get B.
explanation.definitionFit: Goofy as an adjective means silly or foolish, close to stupid or witless.

clue.text: Save clumsy boat that's overturned

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word is reversed

parts.note: a tub is a slow, awkward boat

explanation.surface: Rescue an awkward vessel that has capsized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' is not rescue but the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Save as a preposition means except, as does the conjunction-like use of but.

clue.text: Where children may play with spades and where men may work with picks

definitions.text: Where children may play with spades
definitions.meaning: a play area filled with sand for digging with toy spades

definitions.text: where men may work with picks
definitions.meaning: a quarry from which sand is extracted

explanation.surface: Two kinds of digging, one at play and one at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is both a children's play area of sand and a quarry where sand is dug.

clue.text: One can't resist cricketer, needing new opener

indicators.note: needing new opener says the first letter is replaced

parts.note: a fielder is a cricketer in the fielding side

explanation.surface: A batsman cannot get past a fielder, who needs a fresh opening bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like an opening batsman, but it is just the first letter, F, swapped for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who yields gives way, so a person unable to hold out is one who gives in.
